note: Per-ISO holdout markers gating CLAUDE.md rule 22. TWO INDEPENDENT MARKER BLOCKS (owner decision 2026-07-31), selected by the TIER of the year being touched — the gates were previously tier-agnostic, so a single `complete` entry authorized the iterable 2022 validation ladder and the touch-once 2019/H1-2026 locked test alike. `complete` = VALIDATION tier (2022 and its backward ladder 2018/2020/2021): iterable by design, model-SELECTION evidence, NOT training and never quotable as a certified out-of-sample skill number. `final` = LOCKED-TEST tier (2019, H1-2026): touch-once ever, scored EXACTLY ONCE per ISO with the frozen keeper config, recorded whatever it is, and no calibration change may respond to it. An ISO in `complete` but not `final` may spend its validation ladder and NOTHING else. ABSENCE FROM `final` IS NOT A GRANT AND NOT AUTOMATICALLY A PENDING GRANT — read the ISO's `locked_test` note: it distinguishes 'never authorized' from 'authorized once, SPENT, never re-grantable'. Rule 22 splits two orthogonal channels: (1) DATA INTAKE for any out-of-training year is allowed any time, for any ISO, under explicit session-logged owner authorization, validated no-LP only (byte-identity / loader-resolvability — never a dispatch solve); see `intake_log`; it needs NO marker. (2) SOLVE, SCORE and DASHBOARD REGISTRATION of an out-of-training year need that year's TIER marker. The HOLDOUT SPEND FREEZE (frontend/data/backcast/holdout-freeze.json) outranks BOTH blocks and is checked first: while it is active no out-of-training year may be solved for any ISO, marker or not. Enforced by scripts/lib/holdout_policy.py via run_calibration_full.enforce_holdout_year_gate, legitimacy_diagnostics.run_d6_quarantine and audit_keepers. Marker format: "<ISO>": {"declared": "YYYY-MM-DD", "keeper": "<the ISO's CURRENT designated dashboard keeper>", "by": "<session/owner>"}. KEEPER FIELD SEMANTICS CHANGED 2026-08-02 by owner decision D-5(b), signed 2026-08-02 (docs/handoffs/ffr-owner-sitting-2026-08-02.md Addendum C.1) — OPTION B, re-key on promotion WITH per-promotion determination re-verification: the field is no longer a declaration-time snapshot. EVERY keeper promotion in an ISO that holds a `complete` entry MUST (1) update that entry's `keeper` to the newly designated run and (2) RE-VERIFY the entry's `determination` against that run with `python scripts/calibration_verdict.py --run-id <id>` — which reads committed artifacts only and never re-solves the LP — so the marker never asserts a determination that was never scored against the run it names. If the re-verified determination differs from the recorded one, the promoting session records the NEW determination (or, if it is worse, stops and escalates to the owner rather than silently downgrading a live marker). The declaration-time evidence basis is preserved separately in `keeper_at_declaration`; a SPENT locked-test one-shot keeps its own frozen config in `locked_test_scored_on` and is NEVER re-keyed (the one-shot stands as scored, rule 22). Enforced by scripts/audit_keepers.py check M1, which runs on every keeper-shard edit via the calibration-keeper-auditor agent.
